newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Funds set for Liberian election next month.
newsitem.headline: Funds set for Liberian election next month.

text.p: Donor countries have pledged more than enough funds to finance free elections in Liberia next month but the question is whether they can be disbursed on time, Foreign Minister Monie Captan said on Thursday.
Captan, speaking to Reuters after attending a ministerial meeting in Geneva of the Special Conference to Support the Peace Process in Liberia, said the July 19 poll was on track.
More than $13 million has been pledged, including nearly half by the United States, which is helping to finance training and civic education, according to Liberia's Foreign Minister.
"We have firm commitments for funding for the election," Captan told Reuters.
"We have more money than we need. The question is can we get it disbursed on time," he added.
Funds have been announced by the European Union, Taiwan, Ghana and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), Captan said.
The interim government is holding the poll after seven years of war which killed 150,000 and displaced half of Liberia's population of 2.5 million.
Captan said of the elections: "Overall it is very positive. Everything is on schedule.
"The campaign for elections begins on Monday. We expect ballot boxes from the Danish government to come on time."
Ibrahima Fall, assistant U.N.-secretary-general for political affairs who chaired the one-day talks, told a final news briefing that about $14 million had been pledged.
"We have been informed by government sources and U.N. organisations that part of the funds are already available.
"One has to be realistic that a country emerging from war is not completely peaceful and stable. But I think it is legitimately possible to organise free elections in these conditions," he added.
Fall expected 200 observers to be deployed for the poll.

Kofi Annan, warning that peace and democracy in West Africa were fragile, said in a message from U.N. headquarters in New York that "free, fair and credible" elections were the next crucial step to restoring the rule of law.

Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi reported on the peace process and prospects for the poll. Diplomats noted the irony of his taking part in the talks on Liberia's elections on the fourth anniversary of Nigeria's annulled presidential poll.

Participants included member countries of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), donor countries and other U.N. bodies. Foreign Ministers of Liberia, Ivory Coast, Burkina Fasso and Zimbabwe were among those attending.
"We have all been reminded in these last few weeks of the fragility of peace and democracy in West Africa," Annan said, citing last month's coup in Sierra Leone.

"I have just returned from the Organisation of African Unity summit in Harare and I can report that Africa is speaking with one voice in support of democracy and against the rule of the gun," the Ghanaian added.
It was the third ministerial session since last November.
"Your Conference signals the determination to restore lasting security and the rule of law to Liberia," Annan said. "Free, fair and credible elections are the next crucial step in this process.
"If we succeed -- as I am confident we will -- Liberia can become a model of post-conflict reconstruction involving national leaders, regional organisations and the United Nations.
"The hopes of the continent are with you," Annan concluded.
